title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol: Arminius's own definition — faith prepared in predestination before foresight
pass_a_gloss: Arminius himself, if he wished to be consistent with himself, could not deny that God by this love of election or predestination embraces the elect and predestinated before all foresight of faith in them. For in the Public Disputations, Thesis 15, On predestination, p. 153, he defines predestination thus: It is the decree of the good pleasure of God in Christ by which he has from eternity determined with himself to justify, adopt, gift with eternal life, &c., the faithful whom he has decreed to gift with faith. And in the Examination of the Perkinsian Predestination he grants that God does not foreknow men as about to believe before he has predestinated them that they may believe, p. 32. And he adds this reason, excellent indeed and most valid: For he foreknew, he says, that they would believe by his gift, which gift is prepared in predestination, p. 37. And hither also looks that elsewhere he puts a double matter of predestination: Divine things (which are contained under the name of spiritual blessings) and persons to whom the communication of those is predestinated by this decree. I ask, How does God elect and predestinate from foresight of men's faith, if in election or predestination itself the gift of faith is decreed and prepared for men? For it is ridiculous to say that God in election decrees and prepares faith for certain men, and yet elects the same men from an antecedent intuition of faith preceding this very election; as if God then at last decreed the gift of faith to this or that singular person, when beforehand he had perceived that he would believe.
pass_b_english: Arminius himself, if consistent, could not deny that by this election/predestination love God embraces the elect before all foresight of faith in them. In Public Disputations, Thesis 15 On predestination (p. 153), he defines: it is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ by which from eternity he determined to justify, adopt, and gift eternal life to the faithful whom he decreed to gift with faith. In the Examination of Perkinsian Predestination he grants God does not foreknow men as about to believe before he has predestinated them to believe (p. 32), and adds the strong reason: he foreknew they would believe by his gift, which gift is prepared in predestination (p. 37). Elsewhere he puts a double matter of predestination: divine things (spiritual blessings) and the persons to whom their communication is predestinated. I ask: how does God elect from foresight of faith if in election itself the gift of faith is decreed and prepared for men? It is ridiculous to say he decrees and prepares faith for certain men in election, yet elects them from an antecedent intuition of faith preceding that election — as if he only then decreed the gift of faith to this or that person when he had already seen he would believe.
source_text: Ipse Arminius, si sibi constare vellet, non posset inficias ire, Deum hoc amore electionis sive praedestinationis complecti electos et praedestinatos ante omnem fidei in illis praevisionem. Nam in Disputationibus publicis, Thes. 15, De praedestinatione, pag. 153, praedestinationem sic definit, Est decretum beneplaciti Dei in Christo quo apud se ab aeterno statuit fideles, quos fide donare decrevit, justificare, adoptare, vita aeterna donare, &c. Et in Examine Praedest. Perkins. concedit Deum non praescire homines crediturus priusquam praedestinaverit ut credant, pag. 32. Atque adjungit hanc rationem optimam sane et validissimam, Praescivit enim, inquit, eos suo dono crediturus, quod donum in praedestinatione praeparatum est, pag. 37. Atque huc etiam spectat quod alibi materiam praedestinationis duplicem ponit: Res divinas (quae benedictionum spiritualium nomine continentur) et personas quibus illarum communicatio est hoc decreto praedestinata. Quaero, Quomodo Deus eligit et praedestinat ex praevisa hominum fide, si in ipsa electione sive praedestinatione donum fidei sit hominibus decretum et praeparatum? Ridiculum est enim dicere, Deum in electione decernere et praeparare fidem certis hominibus, et tamen eosdem homines eligere ex antecedente intuitu fidei hanc ipsam electionem praecedentis; quasi Deus tum demum decerneret donum fidei huic aut illi singulari personae, quando antea perspexerit illum crediturum.
